ny_z_loft.blurb: Z-Loft is a lightly developed cliff band in New York that runs for about a quarter mile, with climbable rock reaching somewhere between 75 and 100 feet in places. Chimneys, overhangs and blank faces break up the wall, and boulders sit along the path beneath it. The 15 climbs split between roughly seven boulder problems, mostly easy to moderate with one much harder line, and eight roped climbs from a scramble through about 5.10, done on gear or from a top rope. Expect moss, loose rock and plenty of unfinished work, so a first visit is best spent on a top rope with a crash pad for the boulders.

ny_nameless_area.blurb: Nameless Area is a cluster of boulders at the far end of the Trapps boulder zone in the Gunks, beside the carriage road toward Skytop. The hard quartz conglomerate gives 14 problems, nearly all on the large boulder the area is named for. Grades run from V0 up to a single V9, with the bulk sitting in the easy-to-moderate range and a handful of serious V5 to V8 lines for strong climbers. It is a walk of roughly twenty minutes or more from the Trapps bridge, which keeps it quieter than the roadside boulders closer in, and it suits a morning of traverses with a few pads.

ny_4_nechtanc.blurb: Nechtanc is a small cliff in the Kittatinny section of the Powerlinez, about 40 feet tall and covered in assorted features. The main face looks southwest, while the left end turns northwest and offers shadier climbing earlier in the day. Fourteen routes, almost all top rope with a pair of trad lines, span about 5.6 to the low 5.11 range, with a good spread in the 5.8 to 5.10 middle. It sits only a couple of minutes off the main trail. Rock can be loose, so keep belayers and spectators clear of the base, and scramble around the right side to set anchors.

ny_4_adventure_stories.blurb: Adventure Stories is the northwestern-most sector of the Books Tier at the Powerlinez. Its cliffs run 50 to 80 feet and mix slabs, overhangs and roofs, and most faces look south-southwest. Fourteen climbs are split between trad and top rope, from easy third and fourth class scrambles through moderate 5.8s and 5.9s to a couple of 5.10 and 5.11 lines. The rock has seen little traffic, so expect loose or brittle patches, plus grass, moss and lichen that can slicken holds. Getting here takes a steep scramble from neighbouring sectors, so it suits those comfortable with rough ground, and belayers should stand well back.

ny_8_west_terrace.blurb: West Terrace is a slabby cliff at the Powerlinez, the westernmost of its sunny viewing platforms and part of the Rock Dojo top-rope zone. Slab climbing is the theme, from very easy beginner lines up through the 5.6 and 5.7 range to a few 5.10 and 5.11 climbs. Twelve of the 14 routes are top rope, two are trad. Getting to the top and bottom of the cliff is awkward, so many parties send one person up with the anchor gear and rappel down. A static line of around 50 feet is useful for anchors. Rock can be loose, so stay out from under the climber.

ny_5_the_beard.blurb: The Beard is a pair of boulders in the low east end of the Powerlinez, close to the Giving Tree sector. All 14 routes here are top rope, most with two-star ratings, running from very easy 5.3 climbs through a cluster of 5.7 and 5.8 lines to several 5.10s, which makes it a handy place for mixed-ability groups. To set anchors, scramble up the left side of the left boulder to a platform on top, then cross from there to the right boulder. A few routes on the left boulder need cams and nuts to build the anchor. The rock is lightly climbed, loose in places and overgrown.

ny_shit_rock.blurb: Shit Rock is a small bouldering pocket in the Central Park woods, reached by a dirt path into a clearing west of Worthless Boulder. A slab about 17 feet tall, scored with flared cracks, dominates it, and it is tall by park standards, where most boulders are around ten feet. The 14 problems on the schist range from VB to V6, with plenty of easy V0 climbing for mileage on the slab and the harder lines on the rocks around it. A small cave sits to the east and a large overhanging boulder to the west. The spot is secluded and often littered, so check the landings before pulling on.
